summary:
**Conversation Overview**

This conversation is a technical work session in an ongoing multi-chat project called "The Method 1.6," in which Claude serves as a precision executorial assistant to the project owner (referred to as "M"). The session continued Phase R2 of a structured review of a six-volume academic work on atomic spectroscopy and quantum mechanics. Claude's role is strictly to identify and record findings, never to repair errors during the read phase — a standing ruling established in an earlier chat. When M asked mid-session whether errors were being repaired as found, Claude confirmed they were only being identified and recorded per the existing ruling, and M responded "Continue as planned," making no new ruling.

The session executed three segments of main volume §12.11.1 ("The axes, and what each one sees," lines 3032–3176), covering the axis density table, the box-exhaustive closure proofs, a four-cap sweep of the tower at larger electron-shell caps, and the density dichotomy under enlargement. Each segment followed a strict protocol: clerical checks via r2-tools.py, full line reading, pointer resolution to both headings and claims, figure verification, instrument authoring (r2-ch12q.py, r2-ch12r.py, r2-ch12s.py), golden banking, READ file authoring, and census closure disposition. All tower-computable claims were re-measured on all cells using instruments importing r2lib by path. Sixteen numbered findings were recorded across the three segments, including two unstated conditions in the density definition, a figure that does not reproduce on the live text, an internal contradiction about the number of parents of coordinate K, stale percentage figures superseded by later sections, and an axis that rises where the text says all but one fall. The session closed with BUILD103 (3,397,534 B · md5 fcf00e08…), twelve new bundle members, and HANDOFF-28 prepared for chat 77. M's final request was to produce a CLAUDE.md file consolidating all project custom instructions, which Claude created and delivered.

**Tool Knowledge**

Google Drive large-file fetches consistently spill to `/mnt/user-data/tool_results/<id>.json` rather than arriving inline; the correct decode pattern is `base64.b64decode(json.loads(json.load(open(p))[0]['text'])['content'], validate=True)`. Searching by title using `title contains 'BUILDNNN_compendia' or title contains 'BUILD90_main'` with `pageSize 5` and `excludeContentSnippets=True` reliably locates both live bundles without retrieving retired builds. File sizes for the two current bundles are 1,983,081 B (main) and 3,397,534 B (compendia), and both md5s must be asserted before extraction proceeds. The gate script `gate.py` must run `census` before any instrument run, as it refuses to proceed if a pycache or scratch census exists; `members/__pycache__` must be removed with a delete-only call after every instrument run. The `gate.py manifest` command locates the compendia bundle by scanning `/home/claude` for one `BUILD*_compendia` file, so if two are present after a close, the `--comp <path>` flag is required. The `close.py` script requires `--append` to precede `--members` since `--members` consumes all subsequent arguments, and it must print `reverse recovers md5 <old-md5> == old: True` before writing the new bundle.

1	---
     2	name: file-reading
     3	description: "Use this skill when a file has been uploaded but its content is NOT in your context — only its path at /mnt/user-data/uploads/ is listed in an uploaded_files block. This skill is a router: it tells you which tool to use for each file type (pdf, docx, xlsx, csv, json, images, archives, ebooks) so you read the right amount the right way instead of blindly running cat on a binary. Triggers: any mention of /mnt/user-data/uploads/, an uploaded_files section, a file_path tag, or a user asking about an uploaded file you have not yet read. Do NOT use this skill if the file content is already visible in your context inside a documents block — you already have it."
     4	compatibility: "claude.ai, Claude Desktop, Cowork — any surface where uploads land at /mnt/user-data/uploads/"
     5	license: Proprietary. LICENSE.txt has complete terms
     6	---
     7	
     8	# Reading Uploaded Files
     9	
    10	## Why this skill exists
    11	
    12	When a user uploads a file in claude.ai, Claude Desktop, or Cowork,
    13	the file is written to `/mnt/user-data/uploads/<filename>` and you are told the path
    14	in an `<uploaded_files>` block. **The content is not in your context.**
    15	You must go read it.
    16	
    17	The naive thing — `cat /mnt/user-data/uploads/whatever` — is wrong for
    18	most files:
    19	
    20	- On a PDF it prints binary garbage.
    21	- On a 100MB CSV it floods your context with rows you will never use.
    22	- On a DOCX it prints the raw ZIP bytes.
    23	- On an image it does nothing useful at all.
    24	
    25	This skill tells you the right first move for each type, and when to
    26	hand off to a deeper skill.
    27	
    28	## General protocol
    29	
    30	1. **Look at the extension.** That is your dispatch key.
    31	2. **Stat before you read.** Large files need sampling, not slurping.
    32	   ```bash
    33	   stat -c '%s bytes, %y' /mnt/user-data/uploads/report.pdf
    34	   file /mnt/user-data/uploads/report.pdf
    35	   ```
    36	3. **Read just enough to answer the user's question.** If they asked
    37	   "how many rows are in this CSV", don't load the whole thing into
    38	   pandas — `wc -l` gives a fast approximation (it counts newlines,
    39	   not CSV records, so it may over-count if quoted fields contain
    40	   embedded newlines).
    41	4. **If a dedicated skill exists, go read it.** The table below tells
    42	   you when. The dedicated skills cover editing, creating, and advanced
    43	   operations that this skill does not.
    44	
    45	## `extract-text`
    46	
    47	For docx, odt, epub, xlsx, pptx, rtf, and ipynb the first move is
    48	`extract-text <file>`. It emits markdown for docx/odt/epub (headings,
    49	bold, lists, links, tables), tab-separated rows under `## Sheet:`
    50	headers for xlsx, text under `## Slide N` headers for pptx, fenced
    51	code cells for ipynb, and plain text for rtf. Pass `--format <fmt>`
    52	when the extension is wrong or absent (e.g., `--format xlsx` on an
    53	`.xlsm`). If it errors on a file, `pandoc <file> -t plain` is a
    54	fallback; for xlsx/pptx, fall back to the dedicated skill's
    55	Python-based approach (openpyxl / python-pptx).
    56	
    57	## Dispatch table
    58	
    59	Where a dedicated skill is named below, invoke it by name if you have a
    60	Skill tool, or Read its SKILL.md (listed in your available skills, or in
    61	the same skills directory as this file).
    62	
    63	| Extension                         | First move                                           | Dedicated skill |
    64	| --------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------- | --------------- |
    65	| `.pdf`                            | Content inventory (see PDF section)                  | `pdf-reading`   |
    66	| `.docx`                           | `extract-text`                                       | `docx`          |
    67	| `.doc` (legacy)                   | Convert to `.docx` first                             | `docx`          |
    68	| `.xlsx`                           | `extract-text`                                       | `xlsx`          |
    69	| `.xlsm`                           | `extract-text --format xlsx`                         | `xlsx`          |
    70	| `.xls` (legacy)                   | `pd.read_excel(engine="xlrd")` — openpyxl rejects it | `xlsx`          |
    71	| `.ods`                            | `pd.read_excel(engine="odf")` — openpyxl rejects it  | `xlsx`          |
    72	| `.pptx`                           | `extract-text`                                       | `pptx`          |
    73	| `.ppt` (legacy)                   | Convert to `.pptx` first                             | `pptx`          |
    74	| `.csv`, `.tsv`                    | `pandas` with `nrows`                                | — (below)       |
    75	| `.json`, `.jsonl`                 | `jq` for structure                                   | — (below)       |
    76	| `.jpg`, `.png`, `.gif`, `.webp`   | Already in your context as vision input              | — (below)       |
    77	| `.zip`, `.tar`, `.tar.gz`         | List contents, do **not** auto-extract               | — (below)       |
    78	| `.gz` (single file)               | `zcat \| head` — no manifest to list                 | — (below)       |
    79	| `.epub`, `.odt`                   | `extract-text`                                       | — (below)       |
    80	| `.rtf`                            | `extract-text`                                       | — (below)       |
    81	| `.ipynb`                          | `extract-text`                                       | — (below)       |
    82	| `.txt`, `.md`, `.log`, code files | `wc -c` then `head` or full `cat`                    | — (below)       |
    83	| Unknown                           | `file` then decide                                   | —               |
    84	
    85	---
    86	
    87	## PDF
    88	
    89	**Never** `cat` a PDF — it prints binary garbage.
    90	
    91	Quick first move — get the page count and determine whether the PDF
    92	has an extractable text layer:
    93	
    94	```bash
    95	pdfinfo /mnt/user-data/uploads/report.pdf
    96	pdffonts /mnt/user-data/uploads/report.pdf
    97	```
    98	
    99	`pdffonts` tells you whether text extraction will work before you try it:
   100	
   101	- **No fonts listed** (empty table, just the header) → the PDF is a
   102	  scan or raster export. `pdftotext` and `PdfReader.extract_text()`
   103	  will return nothing useful. Go straight to page rasterization or OCR
   104	  — see the `pdf-reading` skill → "Scanned documents".
   105	- **Fonts listed** → there is a text layer; extract it:
   106	  ```bash
   107	  pdftotext -f 1 -l 1 /mnt/user-data/uploads/report.pdf - | head -20
   108	  ```
   109	
   110	The reason to check `pdffonts` first is user-facing: running
   111	`pdftotext` on a scan produces an empty result, and in a visible
   112	transcript that reads as a failed first attempt before you fall back
   113	to OCR. The two-line diagnostic above costs one tool call and avoids
   114	that — you arrive at the right method on the first try, which is what
   115	a user perceives as "it just read my file."
   116	
   117	That also shapes how to open your reply. The diagnostic commands are
   118	plumbing, not content; lead with what the user asked about. On a
   119	scanned receipt that might be "This is a 3-page scanned invoice; the
   120	amount due on page 2 is $1,845.00," and on a digitally-authored report
   121	it might be "The Q3 report runs 28 pages; revenue on p. 4 is $12.3M,
   122	up 9% YoY." What you're steering away from is the "I'll examine the
   123	PDF" / "Let me check if this is extractable" preamble — the answer to
   124	their question is the first thing they should see.
   125	
   126	For anything beyond a quick peek — figures, tables, attachments,
   127	forms, scanned PDFs, visual inspection, or choosing a reading strategy
   128	— go read the `pdf-reading` skill. It covers content inventory, text
   129	extraction vs. page rasterization, embedded content extraction, and
   130	document-type-aware reading strategies.
   131	
   132	For PDF form filling, creation, merging, splitting, or watermarking,
   133	go read the `pdf` skill.
   134	
   135	---
   136	
   137	## DOCX / DOC
   138	
   139	The `docx` skill covers editing, creating, tracked changes, images.
   140	Read it if you need any of those. For a quick look:
   141	
   142	```bash
   143	extract-text /mnt/user-data/uploads/memo.docx | head -200
   144	```
   145	
   146	Legacy `.doc` (not `.docx`) must be converted first — see the `docx`
   147	skill.
   148	
   149	---
   150	
   151	## XLSX / XLS / spreadsheets
   152	
   153	The `xlsx` skill covers formulas, formatting, charts, creating. Read
   154	it if you need any of those. For a quick look at an `.xlsx`:
   155	
   156	```bash
   157	extract-text /mnt/user-data/uploads/data.xlsx | head -100
   158	```
   159	
   160	For `.xlsm`, add `--format xlsx` (same zip structure; only the
   161	extension differs). When you need a structured preview in Python:
   162	
   163	```python
   164	from openpyxl import load_workbook
   165	wb = load_workbook("/mnt/user-data/uploads/data.xlsx", read_only=True)
   166	print("Sheets:", wb.sheetnames)
   167	ws = wb.active
   168	for row in ws.iter_rows(max_row=5, values_only=True):
   169	    print(row)
   170	```
   171	
   172	`read_only=True` matters — without it, openpyxl loads the entire
   173	workbook into memory, which breaks on large files. Do not trust
   174	`ws.max_row` in read-only mode: many non-Excel writers omit the
   175	dimension record, so it comes back `None` or wrong. If you need a row
   176	count, iterate or use pandas.
   177	
   178	**Legacy `.xls`** — openpyxl raises `InvalidFileException`. Use:
   179	
   180	```python
   181	import pandas as pd
   182	df = pd.read_excel("/mnt/user-data/uploads/old.xls", engine="xlrd", nrows=5)
   183	```
   184	
   185	**`.ods` (OpenDocument)** — openpyxl also rejects this. Use:
   186	
   187	```python
   188	import pandas as pd
   189	df = pd.read_excel("/mnt/user-data/uploads/data.ods", engine="odf", nrows=5)
   190	```
   191	
   192	---
   193	
   194	## PPTX
   195	
   196	```bash
   197	extract-text /mnt/user-data/uploads/deck.pptx | head -200
   198	```
   199	
   200	**Legacy `.ppt`** — convert to `.pptx` first via LibreOffice; see the
   201	`pptx` skill for the sandbox-safe `scripts/office/soffice.py` wrapper
   202	(bare `soffice` hangs here because the seccomp filter blocks the
   203	`AF_UNIX` sockets LibreOffice uses for instance management).
   204	
   205	For anything beyond reading, go to the `pptx` skill.
   206	
   207	---
   208	
   209	## CSV / TSV
   210	
   211	**Do not** `cat` or `head` these blindly. A CSV with a 50KB quoted cell
   212	in row 1 will wreck your `head -5`. Use pandas with `nrows`:
   213	
   214	```python
   215	import pandas as pd
   216	df = pd.read_csv("/mnt/user-data/uploads/data.csv", nrows=5)
   217	print(df)
   218	print()
   219	print(df.dtypes)
   220	```
   221	
   222	Approximate row count without loading (over-counts if the file has
   223	RFC-4180 quoted newlines — the same quoted-cell case this section
   224	warned about above):
   225	
   226	```bash
   227	wc -l /mnt/user-data/uploads/data.csv
   228	```
   229	
   230	Full analysis only after you know the shape:
   231	
   232	```python
   233	df = pd.read_csv("/mnt/user-data/uploads/data.csv")
   234	print(df.describe())
   235	```
   236	
   237	TSV: same, with `sep="\t"`.
   238	
   239	---
   240	
   241	## JSON / JSONL
   242	
   243	Structure first, content second:
   244	
   245	```bash
   246	jq 'type' /mnt/user-data/uploads/data.json
   247	jq 'if type == "array" then length elif type == "object" then keys else . end' /mnt/user-data/uploads/data.json
   248	```
   249	
   250	(`keys` errors on scalar JSON roots — a bare `"hello"` or `42` is valid
   251	JSON per RFC 7159 — so guard the branch.)
   252	
   253	Then drill into what the user actually asked about.
   254	
   255	JSONL (one object per line) — do **not** `jq` the whole file; work line
   256	by line:
   257	
   258	```bash
   259	head -3 /mnt/user-data/uploads/data.jsonl | jq .
   260	wc -l /mnt/user-data/uploads/data.jsonl
   261	```
   262	
   263	---
   264	
   265	## Images (JPG / PNG / GIF / WEBP)
   266	
   267	**You can already see uploaded images.** They are injected into your
   268	context as vision inputs alongside the `<uploaded_files>` pointer. You
   269	do not need to read them from disk to describe them.
   270	
   271	The disk copy is only needed if you are going to **process** the image
   272	programmatically:
   273	
   274	```python
   275	from PIL import Image
   276	img = Image.open("/mnt/user-data/uploads/photo.jpg")
   277	print(img.size, img.mode, img.format)
   278	```
   279	
   280	For OCR on an image (text extraction, not description):
   281	
   282	```python
   283	import pytesseract
   284	print(pytesseract.image_to_string(img))
   285	```
   286	
   287	Note: the client resizes images larger than 2000×2000 down to that
   288	bound and re-encodes as JPEG before upload, so the disk copy may not
   289	be the user's original bytes. For most processing this doesn't matter;
   290	if the user is asking about original-resolution pixel data, flag it.
   291	
   292	---
   293	
   294	## Archives (ZIP / TAR / TAR.GZ)
   295	
   296	**List first. Extract never — unless the user explicitly asks.**
   297	Archives can be huge, contain path traversal, or nest forever.
   298	
   299	```bash
   300	unzip -l /mnt/user-data/uploads/bundle.zip
   301	tar -tf /mnt/user-data/uploads/bundle.tar
   302	```
   303	
   304	GNU tar auto-detects compression — `tar -tf` works on `.tar`,
   305	`.tar.gz`, `.tar.bz2`, `.tar.xz` alike. Don't hard-code `-z`.
   306	
   307	If the user wants one file from inside, extract just that one:
   308	
   309	```bash
   310	unzip -p /mnt/user-data/uploads/bundle.zip path/inside/file.txt
   311	```
   312	
   313	**Standalone `.gz`** (not a tar) compresses a single file — there is
   314	no manifest to list. Just peek at the decompressed content:
   315	
   316	```bash
   317	zcat /mnt/user-data/uploads/data.json.gz | head -50
   318	```
   319	
   320	---
   321	
   322	## EPUB / ODT
   323	
   324	```bash
   325	extract-text /mnt/user-data/uploads/book.epub | head -200
   326	```
   327	
   328	For long ebooks, pipe through `head` — you rarely need the whole thing
   329	to answer a question.
   330	
   331	---
   332	
   333	## RTF / IPYNB
   334	
   335	```bash
   336	extract-text /mnt/user-data/uploads/notes.rtf | head -200
   337	extract-text /mnt/user-data/uploads/notebook.ipynb | head -200
   338	```
   339	
   340	---
   341	
   342	## Plain text / code / logs
   343	
   344	Check the size first:
   345	
   346	```bash
   347	wc -c /mnt/user-data/uploads/app.log
   348	```
   349	
   350	- **Under ~20KB**: `cat` is fine.
   351	- **Over ~20KB**: `head -100` and `tail -100` to orient. If the user
   352	  asked about something specific, `grep` for it. Load the whole thing
   353	  only if you genuinely need all of it.
   354	
   355	For log files, the user almost always cares about the end:
   356	
   357	```bash
   358	tail -200 /mnt/user-data/uploads/app.log
   359	```
   360	
   361	---
   362	
   363	## Unknown extension
   364	
   365	```bash
   366	file /mnt/user-data/uploads/mystery.bin
   367	xxd /mnt/user-data/uploads/mystery.bin | head -5
   368	```
   369	
   370	`file` identifies most things. `xxd` head shows magic bytes. If `file`
   371	says "data" and the hex doesn't match anything you recognize, ask the
   372	user what it is instead of guessing.
   373

# r2-ch12q.py — Phase R2, main §12.11.1 "The axes, and what each one sees", first segment (L3032–3090), chat 76.
# The axis table's cells and density column re-measured under the printed definition (L3077–3086: for each axis, over
# every cell of the stage below, count the values of the new coordinate that exact vector coupling realises, divided by
# the values the bound allows — sum over sum), with the loose readings the text rejects printed alongside; the axis-12
# populations Λ₈ / Λ₉ / Λ₁₀ (L3045–3048) and the J_c-realised filter (L3050–3053; Register 434); φ̂(k) as the monotone
# envelope of max 2J (L3070–3071); the 213 φ̂ sites (L3074); the three independence examples (L3087–3089) and the same
# test at every axis; projection exactness (L3086); the constraint graph by stage against Register 1790 and the Figure
# 12.4 caption (DEFERRED); the tight-K factorisation against §12.11.5's 15,150 / 45,450 and L3067's "3.5 %" (DEFERRED).
# LS terms by microstate enumeration (L3059–3063). tower-2.py by path via r2lib. Deterministic (no wall-clock).
import importlib.util, os, re, itertools
from collections import Counter, defaultdict
H = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
s = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location('r2lib', os.path.join(H, 'r2lib.py')); r2lib = importlib.util.module_from_spec(s); s.loader.exec_module(r2lib); T = r2lib.load_tower()
PHI, FMAX = T.PHI, T.FMAX
N = ['n', 'ℓ', 'k', 'q', 'e', 'f', 'g', '2S', '2S′', 'v', '2Jc', '2K', '2J']

# ---- LS terms of ℓ^k by microstate enumeration (L3059–3063): accumulate (2M_L, 2M_S), strip (2S, 2L) blocks from the top
def terms(l, k):
    if k == 0: return Counter({(0, 0): 1})
    orbs = [(ml, ms) for ml in range(-l, l + 1) for ms in (-1, 1)]
    ms_count = Counter((2 * sum(o[0] for o in c), sum(o[1] for o in c)) for c in itertools.combinations(orbs, k))
    out = Counter()
    while ms_count:
        ML2 = max(m for m, _ in ms_count); MS2 = max(sv for m, sv in ms_count if m == ML2)
        out[(MS2, ML2)] += 1
        for ml2 in range(-ML2, ML2 + 1, 2):
            for ms2 in range(-MS2, MS2 + 1, 2):
                ms_count[(ml2, ms2)] -= 1
                if ms_count[(ml2, ms2)] == 0: del ms_count[(ml2, ms2)]
                assert ms_count.get((ml2, ms2), 0) >= 0
    return out
def new_terms(l, v): return terms(l, v) - terms(l, v - 2) if v >= 2 else terms(l, v)   # multiset difference (L3081)
def jc_values(l, k, S2): return sorted({j for (s2, L2), _ in terms(l, k).items() if s2 == S2 for j in range(abs(L2 - s2), L2 + s2 + 1, 2)})
SYM = {0: 'S', 2: 'P', 4: 'D', 6: 'F'}
def name(t): return f'{t[0]+1}{SYM[t[1]]}'
print('== L3059–3063 terms(ℓᵏ) by microstate enumeration:')
for l, k in [(0, 1), (0, 2), (1, 1), (1, 2), (1, 3)]:
    tt = terms(l, k); print(f'   {"sp"[l]}^{k}: {" ".join(name(t) + ("×" + str(m) if m > 1 else "") for t, m in sorted(tt.items(), reverse=True))}  (microstates {sum((2*t[0]//2+1)*(t[1]+1) for t in tt.elements())})')
print(f'   p^2 new at 2: {[name(t) for t in new_terms(1, 2)]} | p^3 new at 3: {[name(t) for t in new_terms(1, 3)]} | s^2 new at 2: {[name(t) for t in new_terms(0, 2)]} (seniority 0)')
print(f'   2S ≤ k at every term of s^1..p^3 (Chapter 7\'s origin): {all(t[0] <= k for l, k in [(0,1),(0,2),(1,1),(1,2),(1,3)] for t in terms(l, k))}')

# ---- φ̂(k) (L3070–3071): monotone envelope of k ↦ max 2J over the parent shells the caps admit (ℓ ≤ 1, k ≤ 4ℓ+2)
mx = {k: max(L2 + s2 for l in (0, 1) if k <= 4 * l + 2 for (s2, L2) in terms(l, k)) for k in (1, 2, 3)}
env = {}; run = 0
for k in (1, 2, 3): run = max(run, mx[k]); env[k] = run
print(f'== L3070–3071 φ̂(k): max 2J over admitted parent shells {mx} → monotone envelope {env} | tower-2.py PHI {PHI} | equal {env == PHI} | already monotone {mx == env}')

# ---- stages
L8, L9, L10, L11, L12, L13 = T.L8(), T.L9(), T.L10(), T.L11(), T.L12(), T.L13()
L9p = [c for c in L9 if c[8] <= 2 * c[5] + 1]
print(f'== L3033–3039 cells: Λ9 {len(L9):,} | Λ9′ {len(L9p):,} (2S′ ≤ 2f+1 cuts {len(L9)-len(L9p)}, all at f = 0, g = 2, 2S′ = 2: {all((c[5],c[6],c[8])==(0,2,2) for c in L9 if c[8] > 2*c[5]+1)}) | Λ10 {len(L10):,} | Λ11 {len(L11):,} | Λ12 {len(L12):,} | Λ13 {len(L13):,}')

# ---- densities, sum over sum (L3077–3086)
spin = {(l, g): sorted({s2 for (s2, _) in terms(l, g)}) for l in (0, 1) for g in range(0, 4)}
num9 = sum(len(spin[(c[5], c[6])]) for c in L8)
assert all(s2 <= c[6] and s2 <= 2 * c[5] + 1 for c in L8 for s2 in spin[(c[5], c[6])])
print(f'== axis 9: realised 2S′ = spin set of f^g by microstate enumeration, summed over all {len(L8)} cells of Λ8 = {num9}; over Λ9\'s {len(L9):,} values → {100*num9/len(L9):.1f}% (printed 63.7) | every realised spin obeys 2S′ ≤ g and 2S′ ≤ 2f+1: True')
print(f'== axis 9′: same numerator {num9} over Λ9′\'s {len(L9p):,} → {100*num9/len(L9p):.1f}% (printed 67.5)')
def v_real(c, mode):
    f, g, s2p = c[5], c[6], c[8]; out = []
    for v in range(s2p, g + 1):
        if mode == 'parity' and (g - v) % 2: continue
        pool = new_terms(f, v) if mode in ('new', 'parity') else terms(f, v)
        if any(s2 == s2p for (s2, _) in pool): out.append(v)
    return out
for mode, lab in [('new', 'terms new at v (multiset difference, L3081)'), ('parity', 'new at v AND v ≡ g mod 2'), ('exists', 'a term of spin 2S′ merely existing at v (the loose reading)')]:
    n10 = sum(len(v_real(c, mode)) for c in L9)
    print(f'== axis 10 [{lab}]: Σ over all {len(L9):,} Λ9 cells = {n10:,} / Λ10 {len(L10):,} → {100*n10/len(L10):.1f}%' + (' (printed 44.7)' if mode == 'new' else ''))
jc_all = {(l, k): sorted({j for (s2, L2) in terms(l, k) for j in range(abs(L2 - s2), L2 + s2 + 1, 2)}) for l in (0, 1) for k in (1, 2, 3) if k <= 4 * l + 2}
n11 = sum(len(jc_values(c[1], c[2], c[7])) for c in L10); n11_loose = sum(len(jc_all[(c[1], c[2])]) for c in L10)
assert all(j <= PHI[c[2]] for c in L10 for j in jc_values(c[1], c[2], c[7]))
print(f'== axis 11 [terms carrying the cell\'s own 2S, L3082]: Σ over all {len(L10):,} Λ10 cells = {n11:,} / Λ11 {len(L11):,} → {100*n11/len(L11):.1f}% (printed 17.0) | every realised 2J_c ≤ φ̂(k): True')
print(f'   [all terms of ℓᵏ, the loose reading]: {n11_loose:,} / {len(L11):,} → {100*n11_loose/len(L11):.1f}%')
def k_num(jc2, f2): return min(jc2, f2) + 1            # 2K from |2J_c − 2f| to 2J_c + 2f in steps of 2
def k_den(jc2): return jc2 + 2 * FMAX + 1
realised11 = {(l, k, S2): set(jc_values(l, k, S2)) for l in (0, 1) for k in (1, 2, 3) if k <= 4 * l + 2 for S2 in range(0, k + 1)}
def axis12(pop, filt=False, fcell=True):
    num = den = 0
    for c in pop:
        for jc2 in range(0, PHI[c[2]] + 1):
            den += k_den(jc2)
            if filt and jc2 not in realised11[(c[1], c[2], c[7])]: continue
            num += k_num(jc2, 2 * c[5] if fcell else 2 * FMAX)
    return num, den
for pop, lab in [(L8, 'Λ8'), (L9, 'Λ9'), (L10, 'Λ10 (= every cell of Λ11, the stage below)')]:
    n, d = axis12(pop); nf, df = axis12(pop, filt=True); nm, dm = axis12(pop, fcell=False)
    print(f'== axis 12 over {lab}: cells × J_c fibre = {d:,} | exact coupling of J_c with the cell\'s f: {n:,} → {100*n/d:.1f}% | filtered on J_c realised: {nf:,} → {100*nf/df:.1f}% | coupling with f_max instead of the cell\'s f: {nm:,} → {100*nm/dm:.1f}%')
n12, d12 = axis12(L10); assert d12 == len(L12)
n13 = sum(2 if c[11] >= 1 else 1 for c in L12)
print(f'== axis 13: realised 2J ∈ {{2K−1, 2K+1}} (one value at 2K = 0): Σ over all {len(L12):,} Λ12 cells = {n13:,} / Λ13 {len(L13):,} → {100*n13/len(L13):.1f}% (printed 64.4) | Λ12 cells with 2K = 0: {sum(1 for c in L12 if c[11]==0):,}')
print(f'== L3084–3085 the six, under the definition: {100*num9/len(L9):.1f}, {100*num9/len(L9p):.1f}, {100*sum(len(v_real(c,"new")) for c in L9)/len(L10):.1f}, {100*n11/len(L11):.1f}, {100*n12/len(L12):.1f}, {100*n13/len(L13):.1f}  (printed 63.7, 67.5, 44.7, 17.0, 31.4, 64.4)')

# ---- independence (L3087–3090): at each axis, stage-below cells whose realised set has ≥ 2 values; the three printed examples
p2 = [c for c in L9 if c[5] == 1 and c[6] == 2 and c[8] == 0]
print(f'== L3087 p²\'s ¹S and ¹D share a Λ9 cell (f = 1, g = 2, 2S′ = 0; {len(p2)} such cells) and split at v: realised v {v_real(p2[0], "new")} (¹S new at 0, ¹D new at 2) | seniority of p² terms: ' + ', '.join(f'{name(t)} v={v}' for v in (0, 2) for t in new_terms(1, v) if t in terms(1, 2)))
p1 = [c for c in L10 if c[1] == 1 and c[2] == 1 and c[7] == 1]
print(f'== L3088 p¹\'s ²P shares a Λ10 cell ({len(p1)} cells with ℓ = 1, k = 1, 2S = 1) and splits at J_c: realised 2J_c {jc_values(1, 1, 1)} | every K > 0 cell of Λ12 splits at J (2 values): {sum(1 for c in L12 if c[11] >= 1):,} cells, {sum(1 for c in L12 if c[11] == 0):,} at K = 0 with one value')
ind = {9: sum(1 for c in L8 if len(spin[(c[5], c[6])]) >= 2), 10: sum(1 for c in L9 if len(v_real(c, 'new')) >= 2), 11: sum(1 for c in L10 if len(jc_values(c[1], c[2], c[7])) >= 2),
       12: sum(1 for c in L11 if k_num(c[10], 2 * c[5]) >= 2), 13: sum(1 for c in L12 if c[11] >= 1)}
print(f'== independence at every axis (stage-below cells whose realised set has ≥ 2 values, i.e. the new coordinate is no function of those below): {ind} of {len(L8)}/{len(L9):,}/{len(L10):,}/{len(L11):,}/{len(L12):,}')

# ---- projection exactness (L3086): every stage projects exactly onto the one below
print(f'== L3086 projections: Λ9→Λ8 {set(c[:8] for c in L9) == set(L8)} | Λ9′→Λ8 {set(c[:8] for c in L9p) == set(L8)} | Λ10→Λ9 {set(c[:9] for c in L10) == set(L9)} | Λ11→Λ10 {set(c[:10] for c in L11) == set(L10)} | Λ12→Λ11 {set(c[:11] for c in L12) == set(L11)} | Λ13→Λ12 {set(c[:12] for c in L13) == set(L12)} (closure E = 0 at all seven stages: r2-ch12n, banked)')

# ---- L3074 "a symbol used 213 times": φ̂ sites
main = r2lib.read_member('The_Method_1_6-2.md')
cnt = {k: r2lib.read_member(v).count('φ̂') for k, v in [('main', 'The_Method_1_6-2.md'), ('reg', 'The_Method_1_6___The_Register-2.md'), ('mc', 'The_Method_1_6___Mathematical_Compendium-2.md'), ('pc', 'The_Method_1_6___The_Physics_Compendium-2.md'), ('ioi', 'The_Method_1_6___The_Index_of_Indices-2.md'), ('sc', 'The_Method_1_6___Spectra_Compendium-2.md')]}
print(f'== L3074 φ̂ occurrences: main {cnt["main"]} (printed 213; lines carrying it {sum(1 for l in main.split(chr(10)) if "φ̂" in l)}); by volume {cnt}; the occupancy sense φ̂(k) {main.count("φ̂(k)")}, the pairwise sense φ̂ᵢⱼ {main.count("φ̂ᵢⱼ")}')

# ---- constraint graph by stage (DEFERRED: L2406–2408, Figure 12.4 caption, Register 1790's 13 nodes / 14 edges)
E8 = [(0, 1), (1, 2), (2, 3), (2, 7), (4, 5), (5, 6), (3, 6)]                       # ℓ ≤ n−1, k ≤ 4ℓ+2, q ≤ k, 2S ≤ k, f ≤ e−1, g ≤ 4f+2, g ≤ q
ADD = {9: [(6, 8)], 10: [(8, 9), (6, 9)], 11: [(2, 10)], 12: [(10, 11)], 13: [(11, 12)]}  # 2S′ ≤ g; 2S′ ≤ v ≤ g; 2J_c ≤ φ̂(k); 2K ≤ 2J_c + 2f_max (f_max the cap, one parent); |2J − 2K| ≤ 1
def graph_stats(nv, edges):
    tri = sum(1 for a, b, c in itertools.combinations(range(nv), 3) if {(a, b), (b, c), (a, c)} <= {tuple(sorted(e)) for e in edges})
    return len(edges), len(edges) - nv + 1, tri, r2lib.is_tree(nv, edges)
for label, bridge in [('as the table\'s bounds define it (f_max a constant)', []), ('with the f–K bridge added (K read with two parents)', [(5, 11)])]:
    rows = []; E = list(E8)
    for d in range(8, 14):
        E = E + ADD.get(d, []) + (bridge if d == 12 else [])
        ne, rank, tri, tree = graph_stats(d, E); rows.append(f'Λ{d}: {d} nodes {ne} edges rank {rank} triangles {tri} tree {tree}')
    print(f'== constraint graph {label}: ' + ' | '.join(rows))
print('   Register 1790 (measured there): 13 nodes, 14 edges, cycle rank 0, 0, 1, 1, 2, 2, one triangle 2S′–g–v from Λ10, second cycle 2Jc–2K–f–g–q–k at Λ12; L3066: the f_max bound "has one parent and preserves the tree"; Figure 12.4 caption: "constraint tree … the forbidden f···K bridge dashed"; L2407: "B runs e–f–g–v–2S′" (no g–2S′ edge named).')

# ---- factorisation over the transfer (§12.11.5 L3463–3477; L3067 "3.5 %"; Figure 12.4 caption "priced at 3.5 %")
A_IDX, B_IDX = (0, 1, 2, 7, 10, 11, 12), (4, 5, 6, 8, 9)
def factor(cells, d):
    a = tuple(i for i in A_IDX if i < d); b = tuple(i for i in B_IDX if i < d)
    byq = defaultdict(list)
    for c in cells: byq[c[3]].append(c)
    sec = [len(byq[q]) for q in range(4)]; prod = [len({tuple(c[i] for i in a) for c in byq[q]}) * len({tuple(c[i] for i in b) for c in byq[q]}) for q in range(4)]
    return sec, prod, sum(prod) - sum(sec)
for d, cells in [(11, L11), (12, L12), (13, L13)]:
    sec, prod, dft = factor(cells, d); print(f'== §12.11.5 factorisation at Λ{d} (loose K): sections {sec} sum {sum(sec):,} | Σ_q |A(q)|·|B(q)| {sum(prod):,} | defect {dft}')
tight12 = [c for c in L12 if c[11] <= c[10] + 2 * c[5]]; tight13 = [c for c in L13 if c[11] <= c[10] + 2 * c[5]]
for d, cells in [(12, tight12), (13, tight13)]:

# r2-ch12q.py — Phase R2, main §12.11.1 "The axes, and what each one sees", first segment (L3032–3090), chat 76.
# The axis table's cells and density column re-measured under the printed definition (L3077–3086: for each axis, over
# every cell of the stage below, count the values of the new coordinate that exact vector coupling realises, divided by
# the values the bound allows — sum over sum), with the loose readings the text rejects printed alongside; the axis-12
# populations Λ₈ / Λ₉ / Λ₁₀ (L3045–3048) and the J_c-realised filter (L3050–3053; Register 434); φ̂(k) as the monotone
# envelope of max 2J (L3070–3071); the 213 φ̂ sites (L3074); the three independence examples (L3087–3089) and the same
# test at every axis; projection exactness (L3086); the constraint graph by stage against Register 1790 and the Figure
# 12.4 caption (DEFERRED); the tight-K factorisation against §12.11.5's 15,150 / 45,450 and L3067's "3.5 %" (DEFERRED).
# LS terms by microstate enumeration (L3059–3063). tower-2.py by path via r2lib. Deterministic (no wall-clock).
import importlib.util, os, re, itertools
from collections import Counter, defaultdict
H = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
s = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location('r2lib', os.path.join(H, 'r2lib.py')); r2lib = importlib.util.module_from_spec(s); s.loader.exec_module(r2lib); T = r2lib.load_tower()
PHI, FMAX = T.PHI, T.FMAX
N = ['n', 'ℓ', 'k', 'q', 'e', 'f', 'g', '2S', '2S′', 'v', '2Jc', '2K', '2J']

# ---- LS terms of ℓ^k by microstate enumeration (L3059–3063): accumulate (2M_L, 2M_S), strip (2S, 2L) blocks from the top
def terms(l, k):
    if k == 0: return Counter({(0, 0): 1})
    orbs = [(ml, ms) for ml in range(-l, l + 1) for ms in (-1, 1)]
    ms_count = Counter((2 * sum(o[0] for o in c), sum(o[1] for o in c)) for c in itertools.combinations(orbs, k))
    out = Counter()
    while ms_count:
        ML2 = max(m for m, _ in ms_count); MS2 = max(sv for m, sv in ms_count if m == ML2)
        out[(MS2, ML2)] += 1
        for ml2 in range(-ML2, ML2 + 1, 2):
            for ms2 in range(-MS2, MS2 + 1, 2):
                ms_count[(ml2, ms2)] -= 1
                if ms_count[(ml2, ms2)] == 0: del ms_count[(ml2, ms2)]
                assert ms_count.get((ml2, ms2), 0) >= 0
    return out
def new_terms(l, v): return terms(l, v) - terms(l, v - 2) if v >= 2 else terms(l, v)   # multiset difference (L3081)
def jc_values(l, k, S2): return sorted({j for (s2, L2), _ in terms(l, k).items() if s2 == S2 for j in range(abs(L2 - s2), L2 + s2 + 1, 2)})
SYM = {0: 'S', 2: 'P', 4: 'D', 6: 'F'}
def name(t): return f'{t[0]+1}{SYM[t[1]]}'
print('== L3059–3063 terms(ℓᵏ) by microstate enumeration:')
for l, k in [(0, 1), (0, 2), (1, 1), (1, 2), (1, 3)]:
    tt = terms(l, k); print(f'   {"sp"[l]}^{k}: {" ".join(name(t) + ("×" + str(m) if m > 1 else "") for t, m in sorted(tt.items(), reverse=True))}  (microstates {sum((2*t[0]//2+1)*(t[1]+1) for t in tt.elements())})')
print(f'   p^2 new at 2: {[name(t) for t in new_terms(1, 2)]} | p^3 new at 3: {[name(t) for t in new_terms(1, 3)]} | s^2 new at 2: {[name(t) for t in new_terms(0, 2)]} (seniority 0)')
print(f'   2S ≤ k at every term of s^1..p^3 (Chapter 7\'s origin): {all(t[0] <= k for l, k in [(0,1),(0,2),(1,1),(1,2),(1,3)] for t in terms(l, k))}')

# ---- φ̂(k) (L3070–3071): monotone envelope of k ↦ max 2J over the parent shells the caps admit (ℓ ≤ 1, k ≤ 4ℓ+2)
mx = {k: max(L2 + s2 for l in (0, 1) if k <= 4 * l + 2 for (s2, L2) in terms(l, k)) for k in (1, 2, 3)}
env = {}; run = 0
for k in (1, 2, 3): run = max(run, mx[k]); env[k] = run
print(f'== L3070–3071 φ̂(k): max 2J over admitted parent shells {mx} → monotone envelope {env} | tower-2.py PHI {PHI} | equal {env == PHI} | already monotone {mx == env}')

# ---- stages
L8, L9, L10, L11, L12, L13 = T.L8(), T.L9(), T.L10(), T.L11(), T.L12(), T.L13()
L9p = [c for c in L9 if c[8] <= 2 * c[5] + 1]
print(f'== L3033–3039 cells: Λ9 {len(L9):,} | Λ9′ {len(L9p):,} (2S′ ≤ 2f+1 cuts {len(L9)-len(L9p)}, all at f = 0, g = 2, 2S′ = 2: {all((c[5],c[6],c[8])==(0,2,2) for c in L9 if c[8] > 2*c[5]+1)}) | Λ10 {len(L10):,} | Λ11 {len(L11):,} | Λ12 {len(L12):,} | Λ13 {len(L13):,}')

# ---- densities, sum over sum (L3077–3086)
spin = {(l, g): sorted({s2 for (s2, _) in terms(l, g)}) for l in (0, 1) for g in range(0, 4)}
num9 = sum(len(spin[(c[5], c[6])]) for c in L8)
assert all(s2 <= c[6] and s2 <= 2 * c[5] + 1 for c in L8 for s2 in spin[(c[5], c[6])])
print(f'== axis 9: realised 2S′ = spin set of f^g by microstate enumeration, summed over all {len(L8)} cells of Λ8 = {num9}; over Λ9\'s {len(L9):,} values → {100*num9/len(L9):.1f}% (printed 63.7) | every realised spin obeys 2S′ ≤ g and 2S′ ≤ 2f+1: True')
print(f'== axis 9′: same numerator {num9} over Λ9′\'s {len(L9p):,} → {100*num9/len(L9p):.1f}% (printed 67.5)')
def v_real(c, mode):
    f, g, s2p = c[5], c[6], c[8]; out = []
    for v in range(s2p, g + 1):
        if mode == 'parity' and (g - v) % 2: continue
        pool = new_terms(f, v) if mode in ('new', 'parity') else terms(f, v)
        if any(s2 == s2p for (s2, _) in pool): out.append(v)
    return out
for mode, lab in [('new', 'terms new at v (multiset difference, L3081)'), ('parity', 'new at v AND v ≡ g mod 2'), ('exists', 'a term of spin 2S′ merely existing at v (the loose reading)')]:
    n10 = sum(len(v_real(c, mode)) for c in L9)
    print(f'== axis 10 [{lab}]: Σ over all {len(L9):,} Λ9 cells = {n10:,} / Λ10 {len(L10):,} → {100*n10/len(L10):.1f}%' + (' (printed 44.7)' if mode == 'new' else ''))
jc_all = {(l, k): sorted({j for (s2, L2) in terms(l, k) for j in range(abs(L2 - s2), L2 + s2 + 1, 2)}) for l in (0, 1) for k in (1, 2, 3) if k <= 4 * l + 2}
n11 = sum(len(jc_values(c[1], c[2], c[7])) for c in L10); n11_loose = sum(len(jc_all[(c[1], c[2])]) for c in L10)
assert all(j <= PHI[c[2]] for c in L10 for j in jc_values(c[1], c[2], c[7]))
print(f'== axis 11 [terms carrying the cell\'s own 2S, L3082]: Σ over all {len(L10):,} Λ10 cells = {n11:,} / Λ11 {len(L11):,} → {100*n11/len(L11):.1f}% (printed 17.0) | every realised 2J_c ≤ φ̂(k): True')
print(f'   [all terms of ℓᵏ, the loose reading]: {n11_loose:,} / {len(L11):,} → {100*n11_loose/len(L11):.1f}%')
def k_num(jc2, f2): return min(jc2, f2) + 1            # 2K from |2J_c − 2f| to 2J_c + 2f in steps of 2
def k_den(jc2): return jc2 + 2 * FMAX + 1
realised11 = {(l, k, S2): set(jc_values(l, k, S2)) for l in (0, 1) for k in (1, 2, 3) if k <= 4 * l + 2 for S2 in range(0, k + 1)}
def axis12(pop, filt=False, fcell=True):
    num = den = 0
    for c in pop:
        for jc2 in range(0, PHI[c[2]] + 1):
            den += k_den(jc2)
            if filt and jc2 not in realised11[(c[1], c[2], c[7])]: continue
            num += k_num(jc2, 2 * c[5] if fcell else 2 * FMAX)
    return num, den
for pop, lab in [(L8, 'Λ8'), (L9, 'Λ9'), (L10, 'Λ10 (= every cell of Λ11, the stage below)')]:
    n, d = axis12(pop); nf, df = axis12(pop, filt=True); nm, dm = axis12(pop, fcell=False)
    print(f'== axis 12 over {lab}: cells × J_c fibre = {d:,} | exact coupling of J_c with the cell\'s f: {n:,} → {100*n/d:.1f}% | filtered on J_c realised: {nf:,} → {100*nf/df:.1f}% | coupling with f_max instead of the cell\'s f: {nm:,} → {100*nm/dm:.1f}%')
n12, d12 = axis12(L10); assert d12 == len(L12)
n13 = sum(2 if c[11] >= 1 else 1 for c in L12)
print(f'== axis 13: realised 2J ∈ {{2K−1, 2K+1}} (one value at 2K = 0): Σ over all {len(L12):,} Λ12 cells = {n13:,} / Λ13 {len(L13):,} → {100*n13/len(L13):.1f}% (printed 64.4) | Λ12 cells with 2K = 0: {sum(1 for c in L12 if c[11]==0):,}')
print(f'== L3084–3085 the six, under the definition: {100*num9/len(L9):.1f}, {100*num9/len(L9p):.1f}, {100*sum(len(v_real(c,"new")) for c in L9)/len(L10):.1f}, {100*n11/len(L11):.1f}, {100*n12/len(L12):.1f}, {100*n13/len(L13):.1f}  (printed 63.7, 67.5, 44.7, 17.0, 31.4, 64.4)')

# ---- independence (L3087–3090): at each axis, stage-below cells whose realised set has ≥ 2 values; the three printed examples
p2 = [c for c in L9 if c[5] == 1 and c[6] == 2 and c[8] == 0]
print(f'== L3087 p²\'s ¹S and ¹D share a Λ9 cell (f = 1, g = 2, 2S′ = 0; {len(p2)} such cells) and split at v: realised v {v_real(p2[0], "new")} (¹S new at 0, ¹D new at 2) | seniority of p² terms: ' + ', '.join(f'{name(t)} v={v}' for v in (0, 2) for t in new_terms(1, v) if t in terms(1, 2)))
p1 = [c for c in L10 if c[1] == 1 and c[2] == 1 and c[7] == 1]
print(f'== L3088 p¹\'s ²P shares a Λ10 cell ({len(p1)} cells with ℓ = 1, k = 1, 2S = 1) and splits at J_c: realised 2J_c {jc_values(1, 1, 1)} | every K > 0 cell of Λ12 splits at J (2 values): {sum(1 for c in L12 if c[11] >= 1):,} cells, {sum(1 for c in L12 if c[11] == 0):,} at K = 0 with one value')
ind = {9: sum(1 for c in L8 if len(spin[(c[5], c[6])]) >= 2), 10: sum(1 for c in L9 if len(v_real(c, 'new')) >= 2), 11: sum(1 for c in L10 if len(jc_values(c[1], c[2], c[7])) >= 2),
       12: sum(1 for c in L11 if k_num(c[10], 2 * c[5]) >= 2), 13: sum(1 for c in L12 if c[11] >= 1)}
print(f'== independence at every axis (stage-below cells whose realised set has ≥ 2 values, i.e. the new coordinate is no function of those below): {ind} of {len(L8)}/{len(L9):,}/{len(L10):,}/{len(L11):,}/{len(L12):,}')

# ---- projection exactness (L3086): every stage projects exactly onto the one below
print(f'== L3086 projections: Λ9→Λ8 {set(c[:8] for c in L9) == set(L8)} | Λ9′→Λ8 {set(c[:8] for c in L9p) == set(L8)} | Λ10→Λ9 {set(c[:9] for c in L10) == set(L9)} | Λ11→Λ10 {set(c[:10] for c in L11) == set(L10)} | Λ12→Λ11 {set(c[:11] for c in L12) == set(L11)} | Λ13→Λ12 {set(c[:12] for c in L13) == set(L12)} (closure E = 0 at all seven stages: r2-ch12n, banked)')

# ---- L3074 "a symbol used 213 times": φ̂ sites
main = r2lib.read_member('The_Method_1_6-2.md')
cnt = {k: r2lib.read_member(v).count('φ̂') for k, v in [('main', 'The_Method_1_6-2.md'), ('reg', 'The_Method_1_6___The_Register-2.md'), ('mc', 'The_Method_1_6___Mathematical_Compendium-2.md'), ('pc', 'The_Method_1_6___The_Physics_Compendium-2.md'), ('ioi', 'The_Method_1_6___The_Index_of_Indices-2.md'), ('sc', 'The_Method_1_6___Spectra_Compendium-2.md')]}
print(f'== L3074 φ̂ occurrences: main {cnt["main"]} (printed 213; lines carrying it {sum(1 for l in main.split(chr(10)) if "φ̂" in l)}); by volume {cnt}; the occupancy sense φ̂(k) {main.count("φ̂(k)")}, the pairwise sense φ̂ᵢⱼ {main.count("φ̂ᵢⱼ")}')

# ---- constraint graph by stage (DEFERRED: L2406–2408, Figure 12.4 caption, Register 1790's 13 nodes / 14 edges)
E8 = [(0, 1), (1, 2), (2, 3), (2, 7), (4, 5), (5, 6), (3, 6)]                       # ℓ ≤ n−1, k ≤ 4ℓ+2, q ≤ k, 2S ≤ k, f ≤ e−1, g ≤ 4f+2, g ≤ q

def graph_stats(nv, edges):
    tri = sum(1 for a, b, c in itertools.combinations(range(nv), 3) if {(a, b), (b, c), (a, c)} <= {tuple(sorted(e)) for e in edges})

    rows = []; E = list(E8)
    for d in range(8, 14):
        E = E + ADD.get(d, []) + (bridge if d == 12 else [])
        ne, rank, tri, tree = graph_stats(d, E); rows.append(f'Λ{d}: {d} nodes {ne} edges rank {rank} triangles {tri} tree {tree}')
    print(f'== constraint graph {label}: ' + ' | '.join(rows))
print('   Register 1790 (measured there): 13 nodes, 14 edges, cycle rank 0, 0, 1, 1, 2, 2, one triangle 2S′–g–v from Λ10, second cycle 2Jc–2K–f–g–q–k at Λ12; L3066: the f_max bound "has one parent and preserves the tree"; Figure 12.4 caption: "constraint tree … the forbidden f···K bridge dashed"; L2407: "B runs e–f–g–v–2S′" (no g–2S′ edge named).')

# ---- factorisation over the transfer (§12.11.5 L3463–3477; L3067 "3.5 %"; Figure 12.4 caption "priced at 3.5 %")
A_IDX, B_IDX = (0, 1, 2, 7, 10, 11, 12), (4, 5, 6, 8, 9)
def factor(cells, d):
    a = tuple(i for i in A_IDX if i < d); b = tuple(i for i in B_IDX if i < d)
    byq = defaultdict(list)
    for c in cells: byq[c[3]].append(c)
    sec = [len(byq[q]) for q in range(4)]; prod = [len({tuple(c[i] for i in a) for c in byq[q]}) * len({tuple(c[i] for i in b) for c in byq[q]}) for q in range(4)]
    return sec, prod, sum(prod) - sum(sec)
for d, cells in [(11, L11), (12, L12), (13, L13)]:
    sec, prod, dft = factor(cells, d); print(f'== §12.11.5 factorisation at Λ{d} (loose K): sections {sec} sum {sum(sec):,} | Σ_q |A(q)|·|B(q)| {sum(prod):,} | defect {dft}')
tight12 = [c for c in L12 if c[11] <= c[10] + 2 * c[5]]; tight13 = [c for c in L13 if c[11] <= c[10] + 2 * c[5]]
for d, cells in [(12, tight12), (13, tight13)]:

print(f'   the withdrawn 2,475 as a share: of Λ12 {100*2475/len(L12):.2f}% | of the tight-K product at Λ12 {100*2475/sum(factor(tight12, 12)[1]):.2f}% — L3067 and the Figure 12.4 caption print "3.5 %"; §12.11.5 prints 21.4 % / 22.8 %')

input.file_text:
# READ-ch12q — Phase R2, main volume §12.11.1 "The axes, and what each one sees", first segment: the axis table, the two conditions, the four terms, the density definition (chat 76)

Member The_Method_1_6-2.md (BUILD90 main, md5 4aef772b…), L3032–L3090 (59 lines, none over 400 characters; the segment ends at the paragraph break before L3092), read in full against tower-2.py (c0bce27a…, whose stage constructions are the table's six bounds with PHI = {1: 3, 2: 4, 3: 5} and FMAX = 1), the Register (434 at R L1611–1613; 250 at R L987–989; 435 at R L1615–1617; 1790, the DEFERRED item), §12.11.5 (L3462–3479), the Figure 12.4 caption (L2531–2533), the §12.7.1 tower amendment (L2405–2408), §7.4 (L1789–1795) and the caps at L1800, §6.1's φ̂ᵢⱼ (L1535, L1540), Theorem 17.1 (L4806–4810), Chapter 7's origins table (L1760), the MC mirrors (MC L1244 "The six axes of the tower"; MC L1736 "The axis density"), the banked r2-ch12n (E = 0 at all seven stages) and the segment instrument r2-ch12q.py (r2lib by path; every cell of Λ₈ … Λ₁₃ and of Λ₉′; LS terms by microstate enumeration as L3059–3063 prescribe). Pointers: §12.11.3, Register 434, Chapter 7, §7.4 (×3), §12.11.5, §6.1, Register 250, §7.3 and Chapter 17 resolve to headings and claims; §14.4 (L3085 "§14.4-admissible") resolves to a heading only — the section is the stub 12h-01 already carries, and L3085 is a further site of it. No lowercase `register NNN` in range. Census rows in range: 1068 (defect), 1069 (not a defect) — CENSUS-CLOSURES-ch12q.tsv.

## A. Deviations (both texts)

**12q-01 · subject matter — an unstated condition in the density definition.** L3080–3082: `seniority at axis 10 means the terms *new* at occupancy v — terms(f^v) less terms(f^(v−2)) as multisets, not merely a term of spin 2S′ existing at v`; L3084: `Under that definition all six entries reproduce exactly — 63.7, 67.5, 44.7, 17.0, 31.4, 64.4`. MEASURED (r2-ch12q, all 1,654 cells of Λ₉): under the definition as written the axis-10 numerator is 1,655 and the density 1,655 / 2,535 = **65.3 %**; the printed **44.7 %** (1,132 / 2,535) requires in addition that **v ≡ g (mod 2)** — a term of f^g of seniority v exists only for v ≡ g (mod 2), which the text nowhere states; the loose reading it rejects gives 69.0 % (1,748). The other five entries reproduce under the definition as written (B). The section's own standard applies: L3041–3043 introduces this passage as localising `conditions that are not stated anywhere`, and this is a third. MC L1736 carries the six figures with `three non-obvious exact sets required` and points to M §12.11.1 — it inherits by pointer.

**12q-02 · figure.** L3074: `renaming a symbol used 213 times is a larger risk than naming the two senses once`. MEASURED: φ̂ (φ + U+0302) occurs **34** times in the main member (29 lines) and 63 times across the six volumes (main 34, Register 7, MC 19, IoI 3); no form reaches 213 — every φ in main, hatted or not, 70; Φ 6; across all six volumes φ 140. INFERRED: the figure may date from an earlier build; on the live text it does not reproduce. Register 250 (`FOUR TERMS … WERE THEMSELVES UNDEFINED. Defined.`) carries no count.

**12q-03 · Register/main — the 12.7 % pairs two populations in the Register.** Main L3051: `12.7% against 30.8%, an eighteen-point gap`; Register 434 (R L1613): `12.7% against 31.4%, and the gap is entirely the double charge`. MEASURED: 12.7 % is the axis-12 density over the **Λ₈** population (976 cells × the J_c fibre = 26,358) with the numerator filtered on J_c realised by any term of ℓᵏ (3,344); 30.8 % is the unfiltered figure over the same population (8,106) — main's pairing is one population, gap 18.1 points. 31.4 % is over the **Λ₁₀** population (the stage below, 70,905), where the filtered figure is **13.5 %** (9,555), gap 17.9. Register 434 pairs the Λ₈ filtered figure with the Λ₁₀ unfiltered one. Incidental to it: the filter that reproduces 12.7 is realisability by *any* term of ℓᵏ; filtering on the terms carrying the cell's own 2S — the set axis 11's own density uses (L3082) — gives 5.1 / 5.2 / 5.3 % over Λ₈ / Λ₉ / Λ₁₀. The double-charge point stands under either set.

**12q-04 · Register 1790 against L3066 (DEFERRED: the Figure 12.4 caption against Register 1790's 13 nodes / 14 edges).** L3065–3066: `**f_max** — the cap on f under §7.4, **not** the cell's own f … the bound 2K ≤ 2J_c + 2f_max has one parent and preserves the tree and the cylinder`. Register 1790: `Λ₁₃'S CONSTRAINT GRAPH IS 13 NODES AND 14 EDGES … cycle rank 2 (0, 0, 1, 1, 2, 2 by stage) … the second cycle, 2Jc–2K–f–g–q–k at Λ₁₂`. MEASURED (r2-ch12q, r2lib.is_tree): the graph the table's six bounds define with f_max a constant — Λ₈'s 7 edges + g–2S′, 2S′–v, g–v, k–2J_c, 2J_c–2K, 2K–2J — has 13 nodes and **13 edges**, cycle rank 0, 0, 1, 1, **1, 1** by stage, one triangle 2S′–g–v from Λ₁₀, no second cycle; adding the f–2K edge (K read with two parents, the tight bound of §12.11.5) gives exactly Register 1790's 14 edges and rank 0, 0, 1, 1, 2, 2. So Register 1790's edge count is the two-parent reading of the bound that L3065–3066 exclude and that the banked tower instrument (FMAX = 1; 70,905 and 199,130 reproduce only so) does not implement. The triangle, treewidth 2 and 1790's conclusion (§21.5.1's one-level shortfall) are unaffected. Recorded with both texts; nothing withdrawn; the record stands until R3 rules which reading 1790 records.

**12q-05 · stale sites of Register 1790's correction (DEFERRED: the tower amendment L2406–2408 and the implied 2S′ ≤ g edge).** L2405–2408: `the object is two caterpillars glued spine to spine at k–q — A runs n–ℓ–k–J_c–K–J with 2S pendant, B runs e–f–g–v–2S′`; L2531: `Figure 12.4. The constraint tree of the full tower: two caterpillars glued at k–q`; L3066: `preserves the tree`. MEASURED: the table's own axis-9 and axis-10 bounds (L3034 `2S′ ≤ g`; L3036 `2S′ ≤ v ≤ g`) put the edge g–2S′ beside 2S′–v and v–g — the B side is not a path and the graph is not a tree from Λ₁₀ (r2lib.is_tree False at Λ₁₀ … Λ₁₃). Register 1790 records the triangle against §21.5.3 and Figure 21.1 only; L2407, L2531 and L3066 are three further sites. Both DEFERRED items closed here.

**12q-06 · stale figure (DEFERRED: L3067's "3.5 %").** L3067: `the same bound written with the cell's f has two parents and breaks the factorisation by 3.5%`; L2533 (Figure 12.4 caption): `the forbidden f···K bridge dashed and priced at 3.5%`. §12.11.5 L3476–3478: `it breaks the factorisation by **15,150 cells at Λ₁₂ and 45,450 at Λ₁₃**, 21.4% and 22.8% of the product — recomputed; the 2,475 previously printed here is withdrawn`. MEASURED (every cell of Λ₁₂ and Λ₁₃): the tight two-parent K (2K ≤ 2J_c + 2f, the cell's f) keeps 55,755 of 70,905 cells at Λ₁₂ and 153,680 of 199,130 at Λ₁₃; the sections' A × B product stays 70,905 and 199,130; the defect is 15,150 = 21.4 % and 45,450 = 22.8 % — §12.11.5 reproduces. **2,475 / 70,905 = 3.49 %**: the "3.5 %" at L3067 and L2533 is the withdrawn 2,475 as a share of Λ₁₂ (INFERRED identification; MEASURED share). No live measurement gives 3.5 %. DEFERRED item closed.

**12q-07 · word (census 1068).** L3055–3056: `Four terms in the rows above are used to define the coordinates and were never themselves defined`; L3068: `Writing f_max without defining it left the book's title resting on an undefined subscript`. MEASURED: L1800 defines f_max as a cap — `(n_max, e_max, ℓ_max, k_max, f_max) = (3, 3, 1, 3, 1)` — 1,141 lines before its first use in a bound (L2941); the other three (terms(ℓᵏ) at L1892, φ̂(k) at L2788 and L2940, microstate enumeration at L1415) have no earlier definition. Three of four, not four; "never" and "undefined" overstate for f_max.

**12q-08 · word.** L3062–3063: microstate enumeration `is the standard construction and the origin Chapter 7 already cites for 2S ≤ k`. Chapter 7's origins table cites `2S ≤ k … vector coupling` (L1760; L1746 `The fourth, vector coupling, yields an envelope: 2S ≤ k`); it does not name microstate enumeration. The construction is standard (B); the attribution to Chapter 7 is not Chapter 7's.

**12q-09 · layout.** L3059–3075 (the four definitions) are four-space paragraphs and render as code; L3033–3039 is a column-dump table. Production.

## B. Verified (all MEASURED unless marked; r2-ch12q.py)

- L3033–3039 cells: Λ₉ 1,654; Λ₉′ 1,561 (the Pauli cut 2S′ ≤ 2f+1 removes 93 cells, every one at f = 0, g = 2, 2S′ = 2 — s² with a triplet); Λ₁₀ 2,535; Λ₁₁ 13,585; Λ₁₂ 70,905; Λ₁₃ 199,130. The six bounds are tower-2.py's six constructions.
- Densities under the definition of L3077–3086, sum over sum (Σ realised values over the stage below / the new stage's cells): axis 9 — the spin set of f^g by microstate enumeration, 1,054 / 1,654 = **63.7 %** (every realised spin obeys both 2S′ ≤ g and 2S′ ≤ 2f+1); axis 9′ — 1,054 / 1,561 = **67.5 %**; axis 10 — **44.7 %** with the parity condition (12q-01); axis 11 — terms carrying the cell's own 2S, 2,310 / 13,585 = **17.0 %** (every realised 2J_c ≤ φ̂(k); all terms of ℓᵏ, the loose reading L3082 rejects, would give 43.1 %); axis 12 — J_c coupled with the cell's f, 22,275 / 70,905 = **31.4 %** (coupling with f_max instead would give 46.8 %); axis 13 — 2J ∈ {2K−1, 2K+1}, one value at 2K = 0, 128,225 / 199,130 = **64.4 %** (13,585 cells of Λ₁₂ at 2K = 0).
- L3045–3048 the first condition: axis 12 over Λ₈ (26,358 values) 30.8 %, over Λ₉ (45,582) 31.1 %, over Λ₁₀ (70,905 = every cell of Λ₁₁, the stage below) 31.4 % — `a third of a percentage point per stage` (+0.3, +0.3) and converging on the stated value.
- L3050–3053 the second condition (the double charge): 12.7 against 30.8 over Λ₈, `an eighteen-point gap` (18.1) — see 12q-03 for the populations and the filter set. §12.11.3 (L3394) resolves; Register 434 states the two conditions.
- L3059–3063 terms(ℓᵏ): s¹ ²S, s² ¹S, p¹ ²P, p² ³P ¹D ¹S (15 microstates), p³ ⁴S ²D ²P (20); 2S ≤ k at every term; p² new at 2 = {¹D, ³P}, p³ new at 3 = {²D, ⁴S}, s² new at 2 = ∅ (¹S of seniority 0).
- L3070–3071 φ̂(k): max 2J over the parent shells the caps admit (s^k, p^k; k ≤ 4ℓ+2) is {1: 3, 2: 4, 3: 5}, already monotone, equal to tower-2.py's PHI. §6.1's φ̂ᵢⱼ(v) = max{xᵢ : x ∈ X, xⱼ ≤ v} (L1535, L1540) resolves — the two senses are as L3071–3073 describe.
- L3086 every stage projects exactly onto the one below: Λ₉ → Λ₈, Λ₉′ → Λ₈, Λ₁₀ → Λ₉, Λ₁₁ → Λ₁₀, Λ₁₂ → Λ₁₁, Λ₁₃ → Λ₁₂ all exact (set equality). `every stage is closed — exhaustively to Λ₁₀, by the §7.3 proof beyond it`: E = 0 at all seven stages, pairwise to Λ₁₁ and by the exact fibre criterion at Λ₁₂–Λ₁₃ (r2-ch12n, banked, record-carried here); §7.3 (L1776) resolves.
- L3087–3089 independence: p²'s ¹S and ¹D share the Λ₉ cell (f = 1, g = 2, 2S′ = 0) — 62 such cells — and split at v = 0 / 2 (¹S seniority 0, ¹D and ³P seniority 2); p¹'s ²P (50 Λ₁₀ cells at ℓ = 1, k = 1, 2S = 1) splits at 2J_c = 1 / 3; every K > 0 cell of Λ₁₂ (57,320) splits at J into two values. `at every axis` (L3087): stage-below cells whose realised set has ≥ 2 values — 78 of 976 at axis 9, 94 of 1,654 at 10, 640 of 2,535 at 11, 4,900 of 13,585 at 12, 57,320 of 70,905 at 13 — so no new coordinate is a function of those below it. Theorem 17.1 (L4806–4810, `adjunction never repairs … a non-closed set cannot be repaired by adjoining any function of its coordinates`) resolves; the "door" is its contrapositive read as a requirement on a new axis (INFERRED reading; the theorem itself is about repair).
- §12.11.5's factorisation with the printed (loose) K: sections 815 · 3,260 · 6,150 · 3,360 at Λ₁₁, 4,095 · 16,380 · 31,950 · 18,480 at Λ₁₂, 11,470 · 45,880 · 89,700 · 52,080 at Λ₁₃, product = count, defect 0 at all three (for the §12.11.5 segment; measured here because L3066–3067 rest on it).
- Register 250 resolves (the four terms defined); Register 435 records the densities' rebuild (`Five of six densities reproduce exactly and the sixth to a rounding`); MC L1736 reproduces (formula and six figures); MC L1244 lists the five coupling coordinates with the same six bounds.

## C. Incidental

## A. Deviations (both texts)

**12q-01 · subject matter — an unstated condition in the density definition.** L3080–3082: `seniority at axis 10 means the terms *new* at occupancy v — terms(f^v) less terms(f^(v−2)) as multisets, not merely a term of spin 2S′ existing at v`; L3084: `Under that definition all six entries reproduce exactly — 63.7, 67.5, 44.7, 17.0, 31.4, 64.4`. MEASURED (r2-ch12q, all 1,654 cells of Λ₉): under the definition as written the axis-10 numerator is 1,655 and the density 1,655 / 2,535 = **65.3 %**; the printed **44.7 %** (1,132 / 2,535) requires in addition that **v ≡ g (mod 2)** — a term of f^g of seniority v exists only for v ≡ g (mod 2), which the text nowhere states; the loose reading it rejects gives 69.0 % (1,748). The other five entries reproduce under the definition as written (B). The section's own standard applies: L3041–3043 introduces this passage as localising `conditions that are not stated anywhere`, and this is a third. MC L1736 carries the six figures with `three non-obvious exact sets required` and points to M §12.11.1 — it inherits by pointer.

**12q-02 · figure.** L3074: `renaming a symbol used 213 times is a larger risk than naming the two senses once`. MEASURED: φ̂ (φ + U+0302) occurs **34** times in the main member (29 lines) and 63 times across the six volumes (main 34, Register 7, MC 19, IoI 3); no form reaches 213 — every φ in main, hatted or not, 70; Φ 6; across all six volumes φ 140. INFERRED: the figure may date from an earlier build; on the live text it does not reproduce. Register 250 (`FOUR TERMS … WERE THEMSELVES UNDEFINED. Defined.`) carries no count.

**12q-03 · Register/main — the 12.7 % pairs two populations in the Register.** Main L3051: `12.7% against 30.8%, an eighteen-point gap`; Register 434 (R L1613): `12.7% against 31.4%, and the gap is entirely the double charge`. MEASURED: 12.7 % is the axis-12 density over the **Λ₈** population (976 cells × the J_c fibre = 26,358) with the numerator filtered on J_c realised by any term of ℓᵏ (3,344); 30.8 % is the unfiltered figure over the same population (8,106) — main's pairing is one population, gap 18.1 points. 31.4 % is over the **Λ₁₀** population (the stage below, 70,905), where the filtered figure is **13.5 %** (9,555), gap 17.9. Register 434 pairs the Λ₈ filtered figure with the Λ₁₀ unfiltered one. Incidental to it: the filter that reproduces 12.7 is realisability by *any* term of ℓᵏ; filtering on the terms carrying the cell's own 2S — the set axis 11's own density uses (L3082) — gives 5.1 / 5.2 / 5.3 % over Λ₈ / Λ₉ / Λ₁₀. The double-charge point stands under either set.

**12q-04 · Register 1790 against L3066 (DEFERRED: the Figure 12.4 caption against Register 1790's 13 nodes / 14 edges).** L3065–3066: `**f_max** — the cap on f under §7.4, **not** the cell's own f … the bound 2K ≤ 2J_c + 2f_max has one parent and preserves the tree and the cylinder`.     for c in L8c:

        n[2] += num10[(f, g)]; dn[2] += B10[g]

    for c in L8c:
        l, k, f, g, S2 = c[1], c[2], c[5], c[6], c[7]; w = B10[g]
        if (f, g) not in SP: SP[(f, g)] = len(spinset(f, g))

        n[2] += num10[(f, g)]; dn[2] += B10[g]
        n[3] += w * JC[(l, k, S2)]; dn[3] += w * A11[k]"""
assert s.count(old)==1; open(p,'w',encoding='utf-8').write(s.replace(old,new)); print('patched')
EOF

# READ-ch12r — Phase R2, main volume §12.11.1 "The axes, and what each one sees", second segment: the ninth axis tightened, the box-exhaustive closure table, the four-cap sweep, the density table at d- and f-shell caps (chat 76)

Member The_Method_1_6-2.md (BUILD90 main, md5 4aef772b…), L3092–L3135 (44 lines, none over 400 characters; S3 opens at L3136), read in full against tower-2.py (c0bce27a…), §6.1's ℛ (L1540: ℛ(X) = {x ∈ ∏ Âᵢ(X) : xᵢ ≤ φ̂ᵢⱼ(xⱼ)}), Theorem 14.1 (L3683, "A.2": X is closed iff X = ℛ(X); Appendix A's table L9947), §15.4 (L4308–4327, propagation along the tree), the Register (249 at R L983–985; 240 at R L947–949; 1790), §32.1.1's referee flag 1 (L8848–8856, L8892), §7.4 and the caps at L1800, READ-ch12q (12q-01, 12q-05), the banked r2-ch12n (the pairwise and fibre-criterion closures) and the segment instrument r2-ch12r.py (r2lib by path; terms/new_terms/jc_values lifted verbatim from r2-ch12q.py; every cell of every stage's ambient box — 47,775,744 at Λ₁₃ — and every Λ₈ cell of the four sweep caps and the three larger density caps). Pointers: §14.4 (L3096 "§14.4-admissible") resolves to the stub 12h-01 carries — a further site; Chapter 15 (L3099) resolves to §15.4's guarantee; A.2 (L3104) resolves to Theorem 14.1 and A.2 (r2-tools' regex does not know Appendix A's item numbers); Chapter 14 (L3117) and Register 249 (L3119) resolve; "Referee flag 1" (L3126) resolves to §32.1.1's item 1 (L8848) and Register 240 closes it. No lowercase `register NNN` in range. Census rows in range: 1070, 1071, 1072 (all not defects) — CENSUS-CLOSURES-ch12r.tsv.

## A. Deviations (both texts)

**12r-01 · subject matter — the axis-10 exact set beyond half filling, and the referee table's axis-10 column.** L3080–3082 (S1): `the terms *new* at occupancy v — terms(f^v) less terms(f^(v−2)) as multisets`; L3132–3134: axis 10 at (4,4,1,6,1) `33.2%`, at (5,5,2,10,2) `28.4%`, at (5,5,3,14,3) `25.9%`. MEASURED (r2-ch12r, every Λ₈ cell at each cap, multiplicity-weighted): the three printed figures reproduce exactly under that definition — which, beyond a half-filled target shell, credits seniorities the configuration does not contain: p⁵'s only term is ²P (seniority 1), yet ²D is new at 3 and v = 3 is counted. Restricting to v ≤ min(g, 4f+2−g) — the bound L3093 itself gives for the ninth axis — the column becomes **31.9 / 26.0 / 22.9**. At the book's caps no cell is affected (the only over-half-filled target is s², where nothing is new at 2): 44.7 stands, 1,132 under both counts. The other five columns of the referee table reproduce. This is a fourth unstated condition on the density definition (after 12q-01's parity), and the one L3093's formula already encodes: counted with it, `the ninth fibre was indexing v` (L3093) is an exact identity — realised seniorities = realised spins — in 36 of 36 (shell, occupancy) cases; counted as L3080–3082 define, it fails in 12 of 36, every one beyond half filling.

**12r-02 · word — "the tree or the tightness".** L3098–3100: `The price is structural: the constraint graph gains its first cycle, f–g–2S′, so Chapter 15's tree-propagation guarantee lapses and must be retested rather than inherited. **The tree or the tightness** — the language offers both only up to 1,561 against 1,654 cells`. MEASURED: Λ₉′'s graph is 9 nodes, 9 edges, cycle rank 1, one triangle f–g–2S′ (as printed); Λ₉'s is a tree. But the loose tower's own axis-10 bound makes the triangle 2S′–g–v at Λ₁₀ (READ-ch12q B; Register 1790), so the tree is lost one stage later whichever ninth axis is chosen, and §15.4's guarantee (`If the constraint graph is a tree … For an index whose graph has cycles, S2 is open`, L4309, L4327) lapses in either case from Λ₁₀. The choice offered is real at Λ₉ only; a further site for 12q-05's class.

**12r-03 · layout.** L3108–3114 and L3130–3134 are column-dump tables. Production.

## B. Verified (all MEASURED unless marked; r2-ch12r.py)

- L3093 the ninth axis's exact set `{g mod 2, g mod 2 + 2, …, min(g, 4f+2−g)}` equals the spin set of f^g by microstate enumeration for every shell s, p, d, f and every occupancy 0 … 4f+2 (36 cases). L3094–3095: p² = {¹S, ¹D, ³P}, 2S′ ∈ {0, 2}; p³ = {²P, ²D, ⁴S}, 2S′ ∈ {1, 3}.
- L3096 containment: min(g, 4f+2−g) ≤ 2f+1 for every (f, g) (min ≤ mean). L3097 Λ₉′ closes at 1,561 cells — by pairwise joins and meets on all 2,436,721 ordered pairs (0 failures) and by the box sweep (ℛ(Λ₉′) = Λ₉′ over its 27,648-cell ambient box, E = 0); the 93 cut cells are exactly (f, g, 2S′) = (0, 2, 2). L3098 the first cycle f–g–2S′ (12r-02).
- L3102–3119 (Register 249) the closure table: |Λ| = |ℛ(Λ)| with E = 0 at every stage, each against every cell of its ambient box — 6,912 / 27,648 / 110,592 / 663,552 / 5,308,416 / 47,775,744 — the box being the product of the value-set sizes (at Λ₁₃: 3·2·3·4·3·2·4·4·4·4·6·8·9); ℛ(Λ) = Λ as sets at all six. This is the box-exhaustive form chat 75 did not reproduce (DEFERRED, chat 75 block: `Register 249's box-exhaustive form not reproduced here`); it now is, and agrees with r2-ch12n's pairwise and fibre-criterion closures. `no stage admits a cell it does not contain` follows. L3103: C(70,905, 2) = 2,513,724,060 (`2.5 billion`), C(199,130, 2) = 19,826,278,885 (`19.8 billion`), unordered. L3116 `Forty-seven million` = 47,775,744.
- L3121–3124 the four-cap sweep, (n_max, e_max, ℓ_max, k_max, f_max) in L1800's order: Λ₁₃ = **199,130 / 4,731,790 / 40,310,170 / 77,083,771** (by fibre sums; explicit enumeration agrees at the first two: 199,130 and 4,731,790), Σ_q |A(q)|·|B(q)| equal at all four, defect zero; Λ₈ there 976 / 5,157 / 19,109 / 35,789. The envelope φ̂ is monotone at all four ([3, 4, 5]; [5, 8, 11, 12]; [5, 8, 11, 12, 13, 13] twice); every fibre is a non-empty range (2S′: g+1; v: g−2S′+1; 2J_c: φ̂(k)+1; 2K: 2J_c+2f_max+1; 2J: 2 or 3), so every stage projects exactly at every cap.
- L3126–3134 the density table: all 24 entries reproduce by multiplicity weighting — (3,3,1,3,1) 63.7 / 67.5 / 44.7 / 17.0 / 31.4 / 64.4; (4,4,1,6,1) 54.2 / 60.3 / 33.2 / 7.0 / 36.7 / 64.5; (5,5,2,10,2) 49.4 / 55.6 / 28.4 / 4.9 / 28.2 / 65.7; (5,5,3,14,3) 46.6 / 53.0 / 25.9 / 4.2 / 22.4 / 66.1 — axis 10 with 12q-01's parity condition and, at the three larger caps, only under the uncapped seniority count (12r-01). `by multiplicity weighting rather than enumeration` is necessary: Λ₁₃ at those caps is 3,490,022 / 297,614,137 / 4,040,079,888 cells.
- Register 240 (`REFEREE FLAG 1 CLOSED. The tower recomputed at d- and f-shell caps and the dichotomy survives both`) and L8892 (`Flag 1 — coverage — is substantially answered`) agree with L3126–3134.

## C. Incidental

- L3122 `φ̂ stays monotone` tests what L3070 defines φ̂ to be (a monotone envelope); the informative fact is that the raw k ↦ max 2J is *not* monotone at the two caps with k_max = 6 (5, 8, 11, 12, 13, **12**: at k = 6 only p⁶ and d⁶ are admitted, both below d⁵'s 13), which is why the envelope is needed at all.
- L3124 `defect zero at every cap` holds for every cap, not only the four: the A-side fibre (2J_c, 2K, 2J) depends on k and f_max only, the B-side fibre (2S′, v) on g only, and Λ₈ factorises over q by construction, so Σ_q |A(q)|·|B(q)| is the count identically. The sweep confirms the construction; `The shape is not an artefact of the book's caps` is true for that stronger reason.
- L8855 (§32.1.1, flag 1): `§12.11.5's four-cap sweep` — the sweep is at §12.11.1 L3121–3124; §12.11.5 (L3462–3479) carries none. A wrong section pointer for the §32.1.1 segment (DEFERRED).
- The Λ₁₃ box's 2J coordinate has 9 values (0 … 8) although no fibre has more than 3; the sweep decides all 9 slices — this is what makes 47,775,744 the honest denominator of "every cell decided".
- L3099 `Chapter 15's tree-propagation guarantee` — §15.4's own retest figures (`0 of 12`, `42% and 25%`, L4317) are Chapter 15's segment; not re-measured here.

# READ-ch12s — Phase R2, main volume §12.11.1 "The axes, and what each one sees", third segment: the dichotomy under enlargement, the tenth's battery, the order of K and J, what the twelfth and thirteenth axes measure (chat 76)

Member The_Method_1_6-2.md (BUILD90 main, md5 4aef772b…), L3136–L3176 (41 lines, none over 400 characters; §12.11.1.1 opens at L3177), read in full against the referee table (L3130–3134, every entry reproduced by r2-ch12r), §12.11.4 (L3457–3460), §12.11.3 (L3394), the Register (240 at R L947–949; 241 at R L951–953; 1790), exclusion (iii) at L6909–6912, §7.4 (L1789), READ-ch12q (12q-01, 12q-04, 12q-05) and READ-ch12r (12r-01), tower-2.py (c0bce27a…) and the segment instrument r2-ch12s.py (r2lib by path; terms/new_terms and L8_at/phi_at/TERMS lifted verbatim from r2-ch12q.py and r2-ch12r.py; every cell of Λ₁₁, Λ₁₂ and Λ₁₃, every Λ₈ cell of the four density caps, and the exact ninth and tenth objects in full). Pointers: §12.11.1 (L3141, a self-pointer — see 12s-02), Register 240 (L3144), §7.4 (L3147), §12.11.4 (L3154) resolve to headings; Register 241 (L3144) resolves; "exclusion (iii)" (L3171) resolves to L6909–6912 (`Systems without interior cells … the levels are 40–50% configuration-mixed with no assignable parent`). No lowercase `register NNN` in range. Census rows in range: none (CENSUS-CLOSURES-ch12s.tsv is a header).

## A. Deviations (both texts)

**12s-01 · subject matter.** L3137–3139: `Every density except the thirteenth **falls** as the object grows, so the envelope gap widens with scale — the price of certainty is not a constant but an increasing function of the index's size`. MEASURED on the table the section prints (L3130–3134; all 24 entries reproduced in READ-ch12r): axes 9, 9′, 10 and 11 fall strictly and 13 rises strictly, but axis 12 goes **31.4 → 36.7 → 28.2 → 22.4** — up 5.3 points at the first enlargement (s, p at k ≤ 6), then down. "Every density except the thirteenth" is five of six on the first step; the widening-with-scale reading holds for the counting axes and axis 11, not for axis 12 across the sweep. 12r-01's corrected axis-10 column (44.7 / 31.9 / 26.0 / 22.9) still falls.

**12s-02 · pointer to a claim that has no site.** L3140–3143: `converging on the ⅔ that §12.11.1 states as its nominal value. The gap between ⅔ and the measured figure was attributed there to the K = 0 singlet`. Register 241: `TOWARD THE ⅔ §12.11.1 STATES AS NOMINAL`. MEASURED (grep of the main member): ⅔ occurs once in the volume — at L3141 — and "K = 0 singlet" twice (L3142, L3168); §12.11.1 states no nominal value for the thirteenth axis and makes no attribution before this sentence. The claim itself is right (B: density₁₃ = (2N − N₀)/(3N − N₀), the K = 0 share falls 19.2 → 18.3 → 8.7 → 5.2 %, the limit is ⅔), but "there" points nowhere on the live text; Register 241 carries the same pointer.

**12s-03 · undefined term and notation.** L3146–3148: `**And two facts of the tenth's battery worth the print.** Its 10-box appears at caps (5,5,2,6) and not at the book's — the known small-cap effect, caught by §7.4's own discipline, as it caught the same absence for Λ₈ and Λ₉`. "10-box" has this one site in the six volumes; no N-box is defined anywhere (the only sense of "box" in Chapter 8 is the bounding box, L1934), "the tenth's battery" names no test, and the cap tuple (5,5,2,6) is four-valued where L1800 and L3121 write five. Unverifiable as written; nothing measured for or against it.

**12s-04 · internal contradiction, and a triangle that is not the printed tower's.** L3152–3153: `K precedes J: K's parents are J_c and f`; L3065–3066 (S1): `the bound 2K ≤ 2J_c + 2f_max has one parent`. The section reads K with two parents here and one there — 12q-04's tension (Register 1790 against L3066), now inside §12.11.1. L3154–3156: `carrying both with all admissible bounds closes the 11–12–13 cycle in the constraint graph — a triangle in both senses at once`. MEASURED: under the table's bounds K has the parent J_c only and J the parent K only, so 11–12–13 is a path (READ-ch12q B: 13 edges, one triangle 2S′–g–v); the implied 2J ≤ 2J_c + 2f_max + 1 holds on every cell of Λ₁₃, but the converse 2J_c ≤ 2J + 2f_max + 1 fails on **10,370 of 199,130** cells — "all admissible bounds" names an object smaller than Λ₁₃, and the 11–12–13 triangle belongs to it, not to the tower whose 199,130 cells the section prints.

## B. Verified (all MEASURED unless marked; r2-ch12s.py)

- L3140 the thirteenth rises 64.4 → 64.5 → 65.7 → 66.1 (record-carried from r2-ch12r) and the mechanism L3141–3143 describes reproduces exactly: with N₀ the K = 0 cells of Λ₁₂, density₁₃ = (2N − N₀)/(3N − N₀) = 64.4 / 64.5 / 65.7 / 66.1 % at the four caps (Λ₁₂ = 70,905 / 1,238,877 / 102,179,658 / 1,370,242,656; K = 0 share 19.2 / 18.3 / 8.7 / 5.2 %), and 66.7 % with no K = 0 cell. Registers 240 and 241 resolve.
- L3148–3150 `the obstruction … moves up one level, onto v itself — v ≡ g mod 2 and the conjugation ceiling, both still outside the language`: the exact ninth object (Λ₈ × realised spins, 1,054 cells) is not pairwise-closed (101,184 join and 101,184 meet failures on 1,110,916 ordered pairs; ℛ adds 491 cells) and the exact tenth (× realised seniorities, 1,132 cells) is not either (144,832 / 144,832; ℛ adds 1,060). The two conditions named here are exactly 12q-01 (parity) and 12r-01 (the ceiling v ≤ 4f+2−g): the section knows them as obstructions at L3149 and omits them from the density definition at L3080–3082.
- L3152–3154 / §12.11.4 (L3458–3460, verified here because L3153 rests on it): the J-set of a channel is the same through K and direct (J_c ⊗ (ℓ ⊗ s), j = f ± ½) in 12 of 12 (2J_c, f) pairs; the J-fibre density is 64.4 % through K (axis 13 over Λ₁₂) and **39.4 %** direct (33,325 realised of 84,490 allowed by 2J ≤ 2J_c + 2f_max + 1 over Λ₁₁; the two-sided |2J − 2J_c| ≤ 2f_max + 1 would give 41.7 %); `25 points` = 25.0. `axis 13 is reachable from axis 11 without axis 12` — the direct set exists at every channel.
- L3158–3159 every f = 0 channel of Λ₁₁ (7,575 cells) has the singleton K-set {2J_c}; L3167–3168 the J-fibre is a doublet at K > 0 (57,320 cells of Λ₁₂) and a singleton at K = 0 (13,585). L3174 `up to one parity point`: the bound |2J − 2K| ≤ 1 admits three values of which coupling realises two — the third is the parity-wrong 2J = 2K.
- L3136–3137 `the counting axes stay exact and all three coupling axes stay envelopes, at the d shell and at the f` restates §12.11.3's classification (Register 240) at the referee caps; the densities themselves are READ-ch12r B. The classification is §12.11.3.1's segment (DEFERRED 12j-01, "three values, not two").
- L3171 `configurations at 40–50% in the book's own exclusion (iii)` resolves to L6912's figure.

## C. Incidental

- L3139 `which no part of this book had predicted` and L3143 `a route the book did not have when it made it` are narrative about the book's history; not testable.
- L3152 `The order matters and is not the order first written down` — the earlier order is not stated; the K-before-J cost is §12.11.4's 25 points (B).
- L3160–3165 (what K measures; when it is a good quantum number) and L3169–3175 (`the only coordinate in the entire tower that nature conserves exactly … by rotational invariance`; `The two ends of the tower trade places`) are physical interpretation, marked as such by their own wording; nothing in them is a tower computation.
- With §12.11.1 read in full (L3032–3176, three segments), the DEFERRED items assigned to it are all closed (READ-ch12q: the tower amendment and the 2S′ ≤ g edge, the Figure 12.4 caption against Register 1790, L3067's 3.5 %); the section's own figures reproduce except the three named in 12q-02, 12r-01 and 12s-01, and its definitions omit the two conditions it names at L3149.

- **Register entries are append-only** — never removed, relocated or renumbered; a superseded entry is corrected by a new entry that cites it; both states are preserved. Moving an entry out is a deletion.
- **When a reconstruction disagrees with the record, the finding is about the reconstruction.** Never withdraw a recorded finding on reconstructed evidence without the original instrument. Never change an instrument to make a discrepancy disappear (G0c).
- **Authorised work is reported done or not done;** a shortfall is named explicitly. Silence is not completion.
- A message containing a question ends at the question mark; the next action is never announced in the same message as a question (G0, highest priority). Rulings are compact numbered lists and take effect without re-explanation.
